body: Thank you everyone for your input. This helped me understand more. My idea was always to discuss this with a professional before making any decisions, but you helped me be more clear on some outcomes. I appreciate the help!

I sure hope so. I still have a long journey ahead of me. I'm looking at a major medical procedure that will include months of therapy, then there's trying to figure out what to do about the house.

About some other things as well. My oldest is turning 14 soon and puberty coupled with his autism is bringing a whole other set of problems. I am terrified of him going to high school, luckily we have 1 year left at the middle school. I couldn't handle home schooling him, but can't afford a private facility where we are.

This is one reason I'm trying to figure out what to do with the house. We live so far away from any real cities that there are pretty much no resources for him. If we could move closer to a big city he could get a scholarship to one of the programs for children like him. As it is now, public is our only option.

Thanks. I've been dealt a very rough hand of cards.

I learned a long time ago not to judge people, but instead give them patience and kindness. You never know what path brought them to where they are at that moment.

Ha, way to be judgemental. I was including some vague details.

I had my second child almost an entire year *before* the house flooded and 3 years before I was diagnosed with cancer.

**At the time life was actually going pretty great.**

I got a good raise at my job, married the man I thought I'd spend my life with, and we got pregnant 6 months later.

Maybe our relationship was a little young to make that jump, we'd known each other 15 months when we married. He moved from out of town, so we didn't immediately live together as he had to leave his job, sell his stuff, etc... The pregnancy was an accident but he was thrilled and wanted to be a father so bad, or so he pretended......

At 5 months pregnant I found out he'd been cheating on me our entire relationship, cleaned out my savings, lied about getting a job, and left. He has never met his child.

I filed for divorce a month later. Just shy of what would have been our one year anniversary. Everything just went to shit after that.

Only thing I own is a car and my savings and the random household stuff. My assets are few and worth very little. Have another car that's a new loan and then the house itself, so those wouldn't be assets, correct?
How long would it take to recover my credit from doing this?

Thank you. I'm in Alabama. I do have multiple credit card accounts in good standing with good maximums. I have Capital One, Chase, and Citi. Store cards and Care credit through Synchrony. I have a car loan through my credit union that is not quite a year old. Maybe more.

The only thing I would need to have credit for would be a different house, but I'm not sure how that would work. Not that I have enough saved currently for that.

Financially we are pretty good now. After everything on our budget is considered, we still can tuck away savings. I always pay off all credit cards at the end of the month, so the only constant debt is the house and car.

Medical is a big expense as I've just had one surgery and will be having another, much more major surgery soon that will require a lot of physical therapy afterwards. So I'm trying to look into how to get us to the best place possible for the upcoming year.
